chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: Tatum as half improviser, half routine
summary: Tatum's numbers were about three-quarters set routine and one-quarter improvisation, so Stewart could predict much of what he played.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now, when you were working with Tatum, did you find him to be -- was -- did you find him to be like an improviser or was he a guy who had a lot of set routines and just tricks that you could begin to predict after a while?

Well, I think you might say he was half and half, improviser and routine, because we had quite a few, the numbers that we played, that we really stuck to the routine of the number. Of course, during the number there was a whole lot of improvisation going on. But the routine was -- three quarters, and the other was, improvisation a quarter at least.

Yeah, because I've known like a lot of guys who are good players. They'll run up on something that they know how to do, and they do that all the time. After a while you know, you can sit right there, and you can almost play it in your sleep because, you know, you get to a certain point (inaudible). But so you -- so now you -- after you guys got out of the -- got out of the arrangement, then are you saying it was then the part that was after the arrangement, that half of that was routines and half of it was improvisation or --
So you could kind of tell. After a while you knew what Tatum would -- you knew to a certain extent.
What he was going to play --
